items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: I’ve had an experience with Larry Ridley, who I worked with

ctx.x: No not me. Just the composer, the artist, I never got into that hardly at all with any people I worked for. Nowadays it’s a complete free-for-all even though the record companies have such a — all the media companies have such a strangle hold on the arts in general and music in particular. I mean but by the same token now there’s the Internet, there’s CD recorders that you can have at home, you have so many little recording studios that people set up on their own who have made a little money. So while on the one…

industry seems to be so much more controlled than ever before, to me, by the same token there are options now that I don’t think there were twenty or thirty years ago, for the individual artist to try to put his work forth. I’ve had an experience with Larry Ridley, who I worked with, and Charles Davis as well, they both made CDs in the past two or three years on their own. And Larry started selling his on e-Bay and he recently told me he was nominated for a Grammy, I don’t know if that’s for this year or last…
Yeah there’s ways to do it.
